newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee down vs fwd dlr, range-bound in spot.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee down vs fwd dlr, range-bound in spot.

text.p: The Indian rupee was slightly weaker against the forward dollar in late morning trade Friday on bank swap operations, dealers said.
They said forward premiums opened higher on account of banks rolling over their swaps but there was little demand from importers.
"At the moment, importers are still waiting and watching," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Forward premiums opened higher as banks rolled over swaps on their foreign currency deposits."
He said premiums were unlikely to move up much further from current levels unless demand from importers picked up.
November-delivery dollars were quoted at a premium of 88/90 paise against Thursday's close of 86/88.
In the spot market, the rupee was ranged after opening lower on a statement by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on Thursday that he would not like a stronger rupee.
Dealers said after opening lower, the rupee had stabilised as corporates had not reacted to Chidambaram's statement.

"We had expected that some corporates would start covering their exposures," said a dealer. "But this has not happened. We are back to waiting for the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) actions to determine the market movements."
He said most of the morning's trade had been in a 35.825 to 35.830 rupee per dollar range.
"The RBI has not come to the market either in spot or forward so far," the dealer said.
In latest deals, the dollar was quoted at 35.837/845 rupees.
